styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hawker stalls, kopitiam coffee and Peranakan classics.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: UNESCO shophouses, clan houses and colonial streets.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Street murals, galleries and old trades in the lanes.

stays.why: Walk to the murals, clan houses and hawker food. Best for first-timers without a car.
Seafront promenade and the famous hawker centre; short ride to the heritage core.
Quieter local area with cafés and malls; between the city and the beaches.
Beach resorts and night market; far from town, so plan on buses or Grab.

food: Eat at hawker centres: char kway teow, laksa, and cendol. Expect roughly RM5–15 a dish; check prices on the day.
Kopitiam breakfast: kaya toast, half-boiled eggs and local coffee. Cheap and quick.
Peranakan (Nyonya) dishes are the local signature: try a set meal in a heritage shophouse.
Gurney Drive hawker centre is busy at night; go early for a seat.
Little India and Chinatown lanes are good for cheap eats. Many stalls close on one weekday; check on the day.
more_time: Penang Hill: take the funicular for cooler air and views. Go early to beat queues.
Kek Lok Si temple in Air Itam is a half-day trip; combine with a laksa lunch nearby.
Beach time at Batu Ferringhi, or a day trip to the national park and beaches on the north coast.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the heritage core, the food and the murals at an easy pace; add a night for Penang Hill and the beaches.

month_notes: January: warm and fairly dry (19 rain days). Good for walking the heritage core.
February: the driest month (15 rain days). One of the best times to visit.
March: rain picks up (23 days). Plan indoor food stops for afternoon showers.
April: wet (28 rain days). Carry a light rain jacket and keep plans flexible.
May: wet (28 days) and warm nights. Short heavy showers are likely.
June: still wet (23 days) but a little drier than May. Mornings are best.
July: moderate rain (22 days). Good window for outdoor sights early in the day.
August: wetter again (26 days). Expect afternoon downpours.
September: wet (27 days). Indoor markets and cafés are good backups.
October: very wet (28 days). Check forecasts before hill or beach trips.
November: the wettest month (30 rain days). Pack rain gear and plan short walks.
December: still wet (23 days) but easing. Warm days around 29°C.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, around 29–31°C by day and 25–26°C at night. Rain is common in every month, heaviest from September to November.

items.title: Hot all year
items.text: Highs stay near 29–31°C and lows near 25–26°C. No cool season; pack light clothes.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: Expect 15–30 rain days a month. Showers are often short and heavy, not all-day.

items.title: Driest window: January to February
items.text: 15–19 rain days. The best odds for dry sightseeing and outdoor walks.

items.title: Wettest: September to November
items.text: 27–30 rain days. Keep indoor backups and check forecasts before hill or beach trips.

items.title: Humidity and heat
items.text: Muggy most days. Walk early morning or evening and rest in air-conditioned cafés at midday.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, a compact umbrella or rain jacket, sandals, and sunscreen.

transit.best: Walk the heritage core and use Grab or Rapid Penang buses for longer trips.

modes.text: No metro or tram on Penang Island. Don't plan around rail.
Rapid Penang buses fan out from Weld Quay via KOMTAR; fares RM1.40–4. Free CAT buses loop the heritage core and modern centre.
Grab is the main ride app. Taxis use a coupon system or meter; agree the price first.
Possible but traffic and parking in the heritage core are hard. Most visitors skip it.
The heritage core is compact and walkable. Link Bike day pass is RM6.
Rapid Ferry links Butterworth rail station to Weld Quay, RM1.20.
